titleEn: Witnessed Collapse in a Gym - Adult Cardiac Arrest, CPR and AED

patient.name: Walter Brandt
patient.affectEn: in cardiac arrest on arrival: motionless on his back on a gym mat, skin grey, chest moving only with the bystander compressions; after ROSC he stays unresponsive (GCS 3, later 4) with slow, inadequate breaths that need BVM assistance
patient.speechEn: no speech at any point - he is unresponsive throughout. History comes from his wife (distraught and tearful, but answers what she is asked) and from the gym staff.

scene.settingEn: Community recreation centre gym in Kamloops, 0715 hrs. Bright, open gym floor; the equipment has been pushed aside and the floor is dry. The patient lies supine on a rubber mat. A staff member is doing chest compressions; a second staff member is arriving with the wall-mounted AED. His wife stands nearby, distraught. Fire first responders are about 3 minutes out; the nearest PCP car is 8 minutes behind you; Royal Inland Hospital is 10 minutes away. One patient.
hazardsEn: none identified - bright, dry, open gym floor with the equipment pushed aside

bystanders.knowsEn: He said his chest felt heavy while he was warming up at about 0700, and at 0710 he grabbed his chest and went down onto the mat. The staff started CPR within about a minute and nobody stopped. History: heart attack in 2021 with two stents, high blood pressure, high cholesterol; he has had angina since 2021 and the episodes were more frequent this past week - he saw his GP two days ago. Medications: metoprolol, atorvastatin and a low-dose Aspirin every day. No known allergies. Toast and coffee at 0630. TRAP: she says "He always said he wouldn't want machines keeping him alive." There is NO written DNR or No-CPR order - if asked for one or for any paperwork: "No. There's nothing written down. He just always said that." She does not ask the crew to stop and does not produce any document.

Saw him collapse at 0710 and started compressions within about a minute; has not stopped since. He has not used the AED yet - his co-worker is just bringing the wall-mounted one over. Will keep compressing until told to stop and will follow instructions exactly.
Brought the wall-mounted AED. Knows nothing more about the patient. Will hold doors, clear space or fetch things if asked.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: AED (yours; the gym's wall-mounted AED is also arriving with staff)
adult BVM with oxygen reservoir and tubing
PCP only: supraglottic airway and IV start kit

dispatchEn: 0715 hrs. Code 3 to a community recreation centre gym in Kamloops. A 68-year-old man has collapsed mid-workout. Staff are performing CPR and the wall-mounted AED is being brought over. Fire first responders are 4 minutes out. Royal Inland Hospital is 10 minutes away; the nearest PCP car is 8 minutes behind you.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: the collapse was witnessed by staff at 0710, bystander CPR started within about a minute, and the caller states the patient is not breathing normally. His wife is on scene.
arrivalEn: Gym staff wave you across a bright, open gym floor; the equipment has been pushed aside and the floor is dry. A man lies on his back on a rubber mat while a staff member does chest compressions; a second staff member is hurrying over with the wall-mounted AED. His wife stands nearby, distraught: "He grabbed his chest and went down." Fire is about 3 minutes out. One patient, no hazards.
firstLookEn: An older man lying motionless on his back on a rubber mat, skin grey. His chest moves only with the staff member's compressions. The AED is just arriving.

primary.locEn: Unresponsive: no response to voice and no response to a painful stimulus (AVPU = U). He cannot protect his own airway.
primary.airwayEn: Airway clear: no vomit, no secretions, nothing in the mouth. He cannot keep it open himself; once the head is tilted and an OPA is sized and inserted, it is tolerated. Keep suction within reach.
primary.breathingEn: DURING THE ARREST: when compressions pause for the check there are only occasional gasping (agonal) breaths - not effective breathing. With BVM ventilations the chest rises when the candidate looks for it. AFTER ROSC: respirations 6 per minute, agonal and inadequate - the breathing must still be assisted with the BVM at 10-12 per minute.
primary.circulationEn: DURING THE ARREST: NO carotid pulse (breathing and carotid pulse checked together, no more than 10 seconds). No external bleeding. Every pulse check before the engine announces signs of life finds NO pulse; a pulse check during the arrest is the circulation assessment, not a vital sign. AED (give the device prompt only when the candidate turns it on and analyzes): first analysis - "Shock advised"; second analysis, after 2 minutes of CPR - "Shock advised". AFTER the engine announces signs of life (ROSC): a carotid pulse check finds a pulse of 108, regular; a weak radial pulse is present. Any analysis after ROSC - "No shock advised".
primary.rbsEn: Modified rapid body survey during CPR: no hemorrhage anywhere; no medical-alert bracelet on either wrist; a chain around his neck carries a medic-alert tag on his chest that reads "CAD - stents". Nothing else of note. Skin is grey, cool and diaphoretic (skin is given automatically during the RBS).

findings.headNeckEn: Small abrasion on the back of the head (occiput) from the fall onto the mat; no depression, no deformity. Trachea midline, no JVD. Medic-alert chain around the neck ("CAD - stents").
findings.chestLungsEn: Crepitus over the sternum, consistent with CPR. Equal air entry with the BVM ventilations. No wounds.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft and slightly distended (air from the ventilations). No other findings.
findings.backEn: Checked during the transfer to the stretcher: no findings.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: No injuries. Radial pulses now present bilaterally.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: immediately post-ROSC - the first set; no vital signs exist during the arrest (CPR and the AED come first)

resp.character: agonal; being assisted with the BVM at 10-12 per minute

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: en route, about 7 minutes after set 1 - improving but at high risk of re-arrest

resp.character: spontaneous but still inadequate; still assisted with the BVM

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: Fire first responders arrive and are ready to help on your direction.
His wife, crying, says: "He always said he wouldn't want machines keeping him alive."
As compressions resume after the second shock, the patient coughs and moves his arm.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge and plan resuscitation equipment to the patient's side: AED, oxygen, BVM, oropharyngeal airways, suction, and the stretcher
triggers: bring the AED, BVM and suction
bring the airway kit and the stretcher
AED, oxygen, BVM, OPAs and suction

expected.actionEn: Assign crew roles before arrival - who takes compressions, who manages the airway and AED - and plan to rotate compressors every 2 minutes
Recognize from dispatch that this is a witnessed arrest with early bystander CPR - a potentially shockable rhythm - and plan to run the resuscitation on scene rather than moving the patient early
triggers: plan to work him on scene

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards (none), environment (indoor, dry), nature of illness (witnessed medical collapse with chest pain - suspected cardiac arrest), people (one patient, bystanders performing CPR) and resources (fire for CPR manpower, PCP car en route)
triggers: nature of illness is cardiac arrest

expected.actionEn: Don gloves and eye protection before taking over patient contact
First look: older man, motionless, skin grey, no chest movement apart from compressions; direct the bystander to continue CPR until your crew is positioned to take over without a gap
triggers: keep doing compressions until we take over
continue CPR while we set up

expected.actionEn: Assess LOC: unresponsive to voice and pain - U on AVPU
Confirm cardiac arrest correctly: assess breathing and the carotid pulse simultaneously, taking no more than 10 seconds, and treat gasping breaths as not breathing
triggers: carotid and breathing at the same time

expected.actionEn: Take over high-quality compressions with no gap: rate 100-120 per minute, depth 5-6 cm, full recoil after each compression, interruptions kept under 5 seconds
Open the airway, insert an oropharyngeal airway, and keep suction within reach; ventilate at a 30:2 ratio with a BVM without over-ventilating
Attach oxygen to the BVM as soon as practical, but never delay compressions or the first ventilations to connect oxygen
Position the AED and analyze as soon as it is available - CPR continues while the pads go on and while the AED charges
Complete a modified rapid body survey during CPR: check for hemorrhage and medical-alert identification, and report the 'CAD - stents' tag
Note the skin: grey, cool, diaphoretic

Verbalize the on-scene resuscitation decision: adult arrest is worked where he lies because moving the patient degrades CPR quality; state the exceptions (paediatric, hypothermia, trauma, treatable causes)
triggers: we work him where he lies

expected.actionEn: Deliver single shocks with CPR resumed immediately after each, and continue compressions while the AED is charging
Recognize ROSC from signs of life, confirm the carotid pulse, and re-categorize as an unstable post-ROSC patient: RTC, ready to load within 15 minutes, AED still attached
Arrange the PCP intercept en route instead of waiting on scene
triggers: meet the PCP car en route

expected.actionEn: Establish the chief complaint from collateral sources: witnessed collapse with cardiac arrest, preceded by chest heaviness
Take the HxC/C from the wife: exact time of collapse, symptoms before it, whether CPR was immediate, and any down time without CPR
triggers: did he complain of anything before

expected.actionEn: Handle the DNR statement correctly: a verbal recollection is not a verifiable DNR - state that resuscitation continues, respectfully, and ask whether any written order exists
Past medical history
triggers: has he had a heart attack

triggers: corner of the mouth to the angle of the jaw

expected.actionEn: Breathing management: two-person BVM technique with visible chest rise confirmed, 30:2 during the arrest, then 10-12 per minute after ROSC without hyperventilation
Post-ROSC bundle: AED left attached, oxygen titrated to SpO2 at or above 94%, patient kept supine and warm, and the crew briefed to restart CPR immediately if the pulse is lost
EMR: Verbalize that supraglottic airways and IV medications are outside EMR scope; transport with the PCP intercept en route
triggers: the PCP will do the IV

expected.actionEn: Reassess ABCs and all interventions after each move and at least every 5 minutes, with the carotid pulse specifically re-checked
Second full set of vitals within 5-6 minutes of the first, with the improving trend interpreted out loud
Continue assisted ventilation while spontaneous respirations remain inadequate at 8 per minute
State the re-arrest plan: if any reassessment finds no pulse, compressions restart immediately and the AED analyzes
En-route hospital notification with the arrest and ROSC summary
Complete verbal hand-off with times: collapse, CPR start, shocks, ROSC, and both vital sign sets
Accurate PCR completed within 5 minutes

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate turns on the AED / attaches the pads and has it analyze the rhythm (personally or by delegating)
the SECOND AED shock of this call is delivered (by the candidate or on their instruction). Record it only for the second shock - not for the first shock and not for an analysis without a shock
candidate treats the occasional gasping (agonal) breaths as breathing - e.g. says he is breathing, puts him in the recovery position, or does not start or continue CPR because of them

AFTER the examiner has described signs of life (coughing, moving), the candidate continues or restarts chest compressions in a later line without first checking for a pulse, or continues compressions after a pulse has been found. Never record this for the candidate line that the signs-of-life description was answering
candidate stops, pauses or withholds resuscitation, or says they will, because of the wife's verbal statement about machines (no written DNR or No-CPR order exists)
candidate moves the patient onto the stretcher or into the ambulance, or starts transport, while he is still in cardiac arrest (before signs of life and a pulse)
candidate stops compressions, or has everyone stand clear / hands off, while the AED is CHARGING (hands-off is correct only for the analysis and for the shock itself)
candidate stops compressions to place the pads, connect oxygen, insert the OPA or suction, or stops them for a pulse/breathing check that lasts longer than 10 seconds
candidate delays the first ventilations (or the compressions) to connect oxygen to the BVM first
after ROSC, candidate ventilates clearly faster than 10-12 per minute (e.g. 20 or more a minute, or rapid continuous squeezing of the bag)
after ROSC, candidate stops assisting the ventilations (e.g. takes the BVM off and switches to a non-rebreather or nasal cannula) while his own respirations are still 6-8 per minute and inadequate
after ROSC, candidate removes the AED pads, switches the AED off or packs it away
candidate verbalizes checking for or seeing chest rise with the BVM ventilations (or another sign that the ventilations are effective)
an EMR-level candidate inserts a supraglottic airway (i-gel, King LT or similar) - outside EMR scope. Saying that an SGA is outside EMR scope, or that the PCP will place one, is NOT this event
PCP candidate stops or delays compressions or the AED analysis to insert the supraglottic airway before high-quality CPR and the AED are established
candidate actually gives ASA to this unresponsive patient (record drug:asa as well). Asking or deciding whether ASA is indicated, or saying it is contraindicated, is NOT this event

drugs.doseEn: WITHHELD in this scenario: 160 mg PO chewed is only for a patient who can chew and swallow - this patient is unresponsive (contraindication: inability to swallow). If it is actually given, record drug:asa and asa-given.

examinerPrompts.locNotDepictedEn: He does not respond to your voice or to a painful stimulus.
examinerPrompts.breathingNotDepictedEn: When compressions pause for your check, there are only occasional gasping breaths. After ROSC his own breathing is slow and agonal - about 6 a minute - and inadequate.

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR owns every life-saving intervention in this call: confirming arrest with a simultaneous breathing-and-pulse check under 10 seconds, uninterrupted high-quality compressions with 2-minute rotations, OPA and suction, 30:2 BVM ventilation with oxygen, the full AED sequence with single shocks and compressions during charging, and the post-ROSC bundle - assisted ventilation at 10-12 per minute titrated to SpO2 94% or above, warmth, AED left attached, and rapid transport with a PCP intercept. Supraglottic airways and IV access are outside EMR scope. No Functional Enquiry.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds a supraglottic airway once high-quality arrest management is established, switching to continuous compressions with asynchronous ventilations, plus vascular access en route after ROSC, and the 9-system Functional Enquiry from the wife en route. The AED sequence, compression standards, stopping rules and post-ROSC ventilation targets are identical to EMR.

sourcePages: Scenario emd-01 (data/practical/emr-medical-1.json): dispatch, scene, primary (agonal gasps, no carotid pulse, CAD - stents tag), transport (shock advised, ROSC after the second shock, RTC post-ROSC), history (wife's verbal DNR trap, no written order), vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing, handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (cardiac arrest); p.11 primary-survey interventions (performing CPR - absence of carotid pulse; ventilating the non-breathing patient; airway maintenance in decreased LOC); p.13 AVPU; p.40 Adult CPR/AED (breathing and pulse checked simultaneously in no more than 10 seconds, gasping = begin CPR, 30:2, AED as soon as possible, contraindication only a verifiable DNR or No-CPR order, stop at signs of life or 30/40-minute rules); p.42 CPR/AED basic concepts (interruptions under 5 seconds, change operators every 2 minutes, pulse check with ROSC, CPR more effective while stationary - intra-arrest transport only for paediatric, hypothermic, traumatic or treatable causes, early CPR and early defibrillation coexist, full recoil, avoid hyperventilation, SGA for PCPs); p.43 Adult CPR/AED basics (rate 100-120, depth 5.0-6.0 cm, single shocks, resume CPR immediately and during charging, valid DNR); p.45 treatable causes, suction 10-15 seconds in the adult; p.50 Oxygen Administration; p.60 Aspirin (contraindication: inability to swallow). Grading criteria p.19 (packaging goal times), p.35 (vitals intervals).
